title: Indices of Words Holding a Letter
statement:
You get a list of lowercase strings words and a single lowercase letter x.

Return the indices of all words that contain x at least once, in increasing order. Each index appears once, even if the word contains x several times.

examples.why: "tree" and "river" contain an r; "sky" does not.
"aa" has two a's but its index is listed once.

hints: Check each word on its own. What built-in tells you whether a string contains a character?
Collect the index whenever the check passes. Walking the words in order keeps the indices sorted.
Stop scanning a word at the first match so it is listed only once.

explain.intuition: This is a filter over indices: keep i when words[i] contains x. Walking the list from left to right produces the indices already in increasing order, so no sorting is needed. A contains-check (includes, in) stops at the first match, so a word with many copies of x is still listed once.
steps: For each index i, check whether words[i] contains x.
pitfalls: Returning the words instead of their indices.
Pushing the index once per occurrence of x when looping over characters by hand, which repeats indices.
Using indexOf(x) > 0 instead of >= 0, which misses words that start with x.

solutions.title: Scan characters by hand
solutions.idea: Loop over each word's characters and record the index at the first match.

solutions.title: Filter with a contains check
solutions.idea: Keep each index whose word includes x.

followups: Many queries for different letters arrive for the same word list. What would you precompute? (26 lists, or a 26-bit mask per word.)
Return the words that contain every letter of a given set.
